(-23) ON MARCH 6, 2004, AT APPROXIMATELY 01:30 EASTERN STANDARD TIME, A AIRBUS A-319-111 AIRCRAFT, REGISTERED AS N922FR, OPERATED BY FRONTIER AIRLINES AS FLIGHT 9992 HIT A JETWAY WHILE ATTEMPTING TO TAXI UNDER POWER FROM GATE #1 AT ATLANTIC CITY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, EGG HARBOR TOWNSHIP, NJ (KACY). THE REPOSITIONING FLIGHT DID NOT HAVE ANY PASSENGERS AND ONLY THE TWO MAN FLIGHT CREW AND TWO FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WERE ON BOARD AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT. THE AIRCRAFT HAD PREVIOUSLY DIVERTED TO KACY WHILE ENROUTE FROM DENVER (KDEN) TO LA GUARDIA (KLGA) DUE TO SEVERE WEATHER. FRONTIER AIRLINES DOES NOT NORMALLY OPERATE INTO KACY AND ASSISTANCE IN GROUND HANDLING WAS OBTAINED FROM SPIRIT AIRLINES. SPIRIT AIRLINES ALSO DOES NOT ROUTINELY HANDLE AIRBUS EQUIPMENT. THE CREW WAS UNABLE TO PROCURE USE OF THE FIXED BASE OPERATOR'S (FBO) AIRBUS A-319/A-320 AIRBUS TOW BAR (MIDLANTIC JET) FOR REASONS THAT COULD NOT BE CLARIFIED DEVELOPED BY THIS INVESTIGATION AND INSTEAD ELECTED TO TAXI WHILE UNDER POWER FROM THE GATE. STATEMENTS FROM SPIRIT AIRLINES GROUND CREW PERSONNEL INDICATE THAT THE CREW WAS UNABLE TO STOP THE AIRCRAFT IN TIME SHORTLY AFTER AN EMERGENCY STOP SIGNAL WAS GIVEN. THIS HAD BEEN GIVEN BY RELAY METHOD TO THE AIRCRAFT MARSHALLER BY A PERSON POSITIONED AT THE LEFT WING. THE PILOT ALSO STATED THAT HIS ATTENTION WAS FOCUSED ON THE SIGNALS FROM THE MARSHALLER WHO WAS CALLING FOR THE CREW TO MAKE A HARD RIGHT HAND TURN AND WHILE DOING SO, FELT THE LEFT WING STRIKE THE JETWAY. THE ON-SCENE INVESTIGATION CONFIRMED THAT THE LEFT WING TIP HIT THE JETWAY CAUSING DAMAGE TO THE LEFT WING TIP FENCE AND LEFT POSITION/STROBE LIGHT ASSEMBLY. FRONTIER AIRLINES MAINTENANCE CONTROL WAS NOTIFIED AND MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED. THE WINGTIP ASSEMBLY WAS REMOVED AND THE LIGHT ASSEMBLY REPLACED. THE AIRCRAFT WAS FERRIED TO DENVER UNDER A SPECIAL FLIGHT PERMIT WHERE FURTHER REPAIRS WERE ACCOMPLISHED. THIS INVESTIGATION IS CONSIDERED CLOSED. THE CONTENTS OF THE INVESTIGATIVE PACKAGE HAS BEEN FORWARDED TO THE OPERATIONS UNIT SUPERVISOR FOR HIS REVIEW AND CONSIDERATION. FRONTIER AIRLINES PERSONNEL AND SPIRIT AIRLINES COOPERATED TO THE EXTENT NECESSARY TO DEVELOP THE AFOREMENTIONED FACTS.

(.19) ON JANUARY 6, 2003, AT 1248 EASTERN STANDARD TIME, AN EMBREAR ERJ-145LR, N16571, OPERATED BY CONTINENTAL EXPR

(.19) ON JANUARY 6, 2003, AT 1248 EASTERN STANDARD TIME, AN EMBREAR ERJ-145LR, N16571, OPERATED BY CONTINENTAL EXPRESS AS FLIGHT 2051, WAS SUBSTANTIALLY DAMAGED WHEN IT OVERRAN THE DEPARTURE END OF THE RUNWAY WHILE LANDING AT CLEVELAND-HOPKINS INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (CLE), CLEVELAND, OHIO. THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE 2 CERTIFICATED AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOTS, 1 FLIGHT ATTENDANT, AND 47 PASSENGERS. INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED FOR THE SCHEDULED, DOMESTIC FLIGHT THAT LAST DEPARTED FROM BRADLEY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (BDL), WINDSOR LOCKS, CONNECTICUT. FLIGHT 2051 WAS CONDUCTED ON AN INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES (IFR) FLIGHT PLAN UNDER 14 CFR PART 121. ACCORDING TO AN INSPECTOR FROM THE FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA), THERE WERE NO REPORTED PROBLEMS WITH THE EN ROUTE OR APPROACH PHASES OF THE FLIGHT. THE ILS RUNWAY 6L APPROACH WAS PERFORMED. AFTER TOUCHDOWN, THE FLIGHT CREW WAS UNABLE TO STOP THE AIRPLANE ON THE RUNWAY. THE AIRPLANE CONTINUED BEYOND THE DEPARTURE END, ON EXTENDED RUNWAY CENTERLINE, AND STRUCK THE ILS RUNWAY 6L LOCALIZER ANTENNA. IT CAME TO REST WITH THE NOSE ABOUT 600 FEET BEYOND THE DEPARTURE END OF THE RUNWAY. THE PASSENGERS EXITED THE AIRPLANE THROUGH THE MAIN CABIN DOOR, AND WERE TAKEN TO THE TERMINAL VIA VEHICLES. THE ILS RUNWAY 6L LOCALIZER ANTENNA WAS LOCATED 510 FEET BEYOND THE DEPARTURE END OF THE RUNWAY. THE ILS DME ANTENNA WAS CO-LOCATED WITH THE ILS RUNWAY 6L LOCALIZER ANTENNA. EXAMINATION OF THE AIRPLANE REVEALED THAT THE TAIL OF THE AIRPLANE WAS ABEAM OF THE LOCALIZER ANTENNA. IN ADDITION, THE NOSE LANDING GEAR HAD COLLAPSED REARWARD AND DEFORMED THE FORWARD PRESSURE BULKHEAD. MINOR DAMAGE IN THE FORM OF SCRAPES WERE FOUND ON THE LEADING EDGE OF BOTH WINGS. ACCORDING TO THE FLIGHT DATA RECORDER, THE AIR/GROUND SQUAT SWITCH ON THE MAIN LANDING GEAR TRANSITIONED FROM AIR TO GROUND WHEN THE AIRPLANE WAS ABOUT 0.38 NM FROM THE ILS DME ANTENNA, WITH AN INDICATED AIRSPEED OF ABOUT 150 KNOTS (KIAS). WHEN THE AIRPLANE WAS ABOUT 0.13 NM FROM THE ILS DME ANTENNA, THE AIRSPEED WAS ABOUT 100 KIAS. AT THE SAME TIME THAT THE MAIN LANDING GEAR SQUAT SWITCH TRANSITIONED TO GROUND, THE SPOILERS DEPLOYED, AND 3 SECONDS LATER, THE THRUST REVERSERS WERE DEPLOYED. AT 1147, A NOTAM WAS ISSUED THAT RUNWAY 6L/24R WAS COVERED WITH THIN WET SNOW. THE RUNWAY HAD BEEN "BROOMED" FULL LENGTH AND WIDTH, AND LIQUID DEICER AND SAND HAD BEEN APPLIED TO A WIDTH OF 100 FEET. "TAPLEY" READINGS AT THE TOUCHDOWN, MIDDLE, AND ROLLOUT ZONES OF THE RUNWAYS MEASURED 60, 60, AND 60. THERE WAS NO RECORD OF ANY FURTHER TREATMENT OR SNOW REMOVAL FROM THE TIME THE RUNWAY WAS OPENED, UNTIL AFTER THE ACCIDENT. THE RECORDED WEATHER OBSERVATION AT CLEVELAND, AT 1242, INCLUDED WINDS FROM 330 DEGREES AT 19 KNOTS, WITH GUSTS TO 29 KNOTS, VISIBILITY 1/2 STATUTE MILE, SNOW, BLOWING SNOW, MIST, BROKEN CLOUDS AT 1,100 FEET, OVERCAST CLOUDS AT 1,600 FEET, TEMPERATURE -3 F, DEW POINT -4 F, ALTIMETER 30.07. AT 1251, THE WEATHER OBSERVATION INCLUDED WINDS FROM 330 DEGREES AT 17 KNOTS, GUSTS TO 26 KNOTS, VISIBILITY 1/2 STATUTE MILE, SNOW, BLOWING SNOW, MIST, FEW CLOUDS AT 700 FEET, OVERCAST CLOUDS AT 1,600 FEET, TEMPERATURE -4 F, DEW POINT -4 F, ALTIMETER 30.07. AT 1259, "TAPLEY" READINGS WERE TAKEN ON THE RUNWAY. THE READINGS VARIED BETWEEN 25 AND 30 ON ALL SECTIONS OF THE RUNWAY. ACCORDING TO FAA DATA, RUNWAY 6L WAS 6,800 FEET LONG, 150 FEET WIDE, AND HAD AN ASPHALT SURFACE. THE LANDING THRESHOLD FOR RUNWAY 6L WAS DISPLACED 530 FEET. THE COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER AND DIGITAL FLIGHT DATA RECORDER HAVE BEEN RETAINED FOR REVIEW. (-23) ON FEBRUARY 14, 2002 AT 14:55 CENTRAL STANDARD TIME, THE GREAT LAKES REGIONAL CONTROL WAS INFORMED THAT SOUTH

(-23) ON FEBRUARY 14, 2002 AT 14:55 CENTRAL STANDARD TIME, THE GREAT LAKES REGIONAL CONTROL WAS INFORMED THAT SOUTHWEST (SWAA) FLIGHT #123, A BOEING 737-7H4 AIRCRAFT, REGISTRATION NUMBER N407WN, HAD IMPACTED A PASSENGER BOARDING JETWAY BRIDGE AT THE CHICAGO MIDWAY AIRPORT (MDW). ON FEBRUARY 15, 2002, THE CHICAGO O'HARE FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE WAS NOTIFIED OF THE INCIDENT. INITIAL INQUIRIES INTO THE INCIDENT REVEALED THERE WERE NO INJURIES AND THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED MINOR DAMAGE TO THE LEFT ENGINE INTAKE COWLING. AVIATION SAFETY INSPECTORS PERFORMED THE ON SCEND INVESTIGATION ON FEBRUARY 19, 2002. A REPORT FILED BY THE PILOT IN COMMAND (PIC) INDICATED THAT FLIGHT #123, ENROUTE FROM JACKSON, MISSISSIPPI (JAN), LANDED AT MDW AND PROCEEDED TO TERMINAL GATE F-18. AFTER TURNING ON THE TAXI LINE TO THE GATE THE PIC FOCUSED ON THE MARSHALLER FOR FINAL DIRECTIONS INTO THE DESIGNATED PARKING SPOT. AFTER SHUTTING DOWN THE ENGINES THE PIC REPORTED HE NOTICED THE LEFT ENGINE WAS VERY CLOSE TO THE JETWAY. AFTER DEPLANING 58 PASSENGERS AND 5 CREWMEMBERS THE PIC TALKED TO THE JETWAY OPERATOR WHERE UPON HE FOUND THE TOP OF THE LEFT ENGINE HAD IMPACTED THE JETWAY. THE PIC INDICATED, IN HIS REPORT, THAT HE DID NOT FEEL ANY IMPACT WHILE TAXIING INTO THE SPOT. IN A REPORT OBTAINED FROM SWAA, THE JETWAY OPERATOR STATED THAT SINCE NEW "AIRCRAFT SAFETY ENVELOPE" AND "STOP MARKS" HAD BEEN REPAINTED AND MOVED APPROXIMATELY 5 FEET CLOSER TO THE TERMINAL THAT MORNING, SHE TRIED TO ANTICIPATE THE AIRCRAFT'S FINAL POSITION RELATIVE TO THE JETWAY BRIDGE PRIOR TO ITS ARRIVAL. THE JETWAY OPERATOR DID NOT REALIZE THE BRIDGE WAS NOT PROPERLY POSITIONED UNTIL AFTER AIRCRAFT CABIN DOOR MOVED PAST THE JETWAY BRIDGE AS THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP. THE OPERATOR ALSO NOTED THAT PART OF THE LEFT ENGINE WAS NOW UNDER THE JETWAY BRIDGE. IN THE ATTEMPT TO PROPERLY REPOSITION THE JETWAY THE BRIDGE SCRAPPED THE TOP OF THE ENGINE COWLING CAUSING THE AIRCRAFT DAMAGE. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY REMOVED FROM SERVICE AFTER SWAA MAINTENANCE INSPECTED THE DAMAGE AND FOUND A 20-INCH LONG BY 1/4 INCH DEEP GOUGE IN TOP OF THE LEFT ENGINE COWLING. SWAA MAINTENANCE PERFORMED A DRAGGED ENGINE NACELLE INSPECTION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE BOEING MAINTENANCE MANUAL. CHAPTER 05-51-10-2, BUT FOUND NO FURTHER DAMAGE. A TEMPORARY SPEED TAPE REPAIR WAS COMPLETED ON THE NOSE COWLING IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SWAA STRUCTURAL REPAIR MANUAL IN ANTICIPATION OF A MAINTENANCE FERRY FLIGHT TO A MAJOR MAINTENANCE BASE. THE AIRCRAFT WAS INSPECTED AND RELEASED FOR A ONE-TIME FERRY FLIGHT TO THE DALLAS LOVE FIELD (DAL) MAINTENANCE FACILITY WHERE THE NOSE COWLING WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED.

(-23) ON OCTOBER 3, 2005, AT 1100 EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME, AN EMBRAER 170, N650RW, OPERATED BY SHUTTLE AMERICA, WAS U

(-23) ON OCTOBER 3, 2005, AT 1100 EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME, AN EMBRAER 170, N650RW, OPERATED BY SHUTTLE AMERICA, WAS UNDAMAGED WHILE CLIMBING TO AVOID TRAFFIC NEAR WASHINGTON DULLES INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (IAD), DULLES, VIRGINIA. THE CERTIFICATED AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOT, COMMERCIAL PILOT, A CABIN ATTENDANT, AND 70 PASSENGERS WERE NOT INJURED. ONE CABIN ATTENDANT WAS SERIOUSLY INJURED. VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED, AND AN INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES (IFR) FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED FOR THE FLIGHT THAT ORIGINATED FROM MONTREAL DORVAL INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (YUL), MONTREAL, CANADA. THE SCHEDULED PASSENGER FLIGHT WAS CONDUCTED UNDER 14 CFR PART 121. IN WRITTEN STATEMENTS, THE FLIGHT CREW EXPLAINED THAT AS THEY APPROACHED THE AIRPORT, ON THE DOWNWIND LEG OF THE TRAFFIC PATTERN AT 3,000 FEET, THE AIRPLANE'S TRAFFIC COLLISION AVOIDANCE SYSTEM (TCAS) PROVIDED A RESOLUTION ADVISORY (RA), AND ADVISED THE CREW TO INITIATE A CLIMB. THE FIRST OFFICER CLIMBED THE AIRPLANE TO 3,500 FEET, AND "ONCE THE RA WAS COMPLIED WITH", DESCENDED BACK TO 3,000 FEET. PRELIMINARY AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL (ATC) RADAR AND COMMUNICATION DATE DEPICTED THE ACCIDENT AIRPLANE ON A SOUTHERLY TRACK AT 3,000 FEET, AND ANOTHERAIRPLANE CONVERGING HEAD-ON FROM THE SOUTH, AT 2,500 FEET. THE CONTROLLER INSTRUCTED THE ACCIDENT AIRPLANE TO TURN TO A SOUTHWESTERLY HEADING, AND THE AIRPLANE ASSUMED A DIVERGENT, SOUTHWESTERLY TRACK FOR ABOUT 10 SECONDS, BEFORE A CLIMB TO 3,500 FEET WAS INITIATED. AFTER THE AIRPLANE DESCENDED TO 3,000 FEET, A CABIN ATTENDANT ADVISED THE FLIGHT CREW THAT THE OTHER CABIN ATTENDANT WAS INJURED. AFTER CONSULTING WITH THE CABIN CREW, THE FLIGHT ELECTED TO CONTINUE THE FLIGHT TO DULLES AIRPORT, AND MEDICAL PERSONNEL MET THE AIRPLANE AT THE GATE. ACCORDING TO THE DIRECTOR OF SAFETY FOR THE OPERATOR, COMPANY MANAGEMENT DID NOT IMMEDIATELY KNOW THE EXACT DETAILS OF THE EVENT, AND THE AIRPLANE WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE. CONSEQUENTLY, COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER DATA FOR THE ACCIDENT FLIGHT WAS LOST. COMPANY PERSONNEL DOWNLOADED THE FLIGHT DATA RECORDER (FDR), AND THE DATA WAS FORWARDED TO THE SAFETY BOARD LABORATORY IN WASHINGTON, D.C., FOR ANALYSIS. THE CAPTAIN HELD AN AIRLINE TRANSPORT PILOT CERTIFICATE WITH A RATING FOR AIRPLANE MULTI-ENGINE LAND. HIS MOST RECENT FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA) FIRST CLASS MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WAS ISSUED APRIL 14, 2005. THE CAPTAIN REPORTED 2,000 TOTAL HOURS OF FLIGHT EXPERIENCE, 173 HOURS OF WHICH WERE IN MAKE AND MODEL. THE FIRST OFFICER HELD A COMMERCIAL PILOT CERTIFICATE WITH RATINGS FOR AIRPLANE MULTI-ENGINE LAND. HIS MOST RECENT FAA FIRST CLASS MEDICAL CERTIFICATE WAS ISSUED ON OCTOBER 6, 2004. THE FIRST OFFICER REPORTED 5,300 TOTAL HOURS OF FLIGHT EXPERIENCE, 453 HOURS OF WHICH WERE IN MAKE AND MODEL. AT 1051, THE WEATHER REPORTED AT DULLES AIRPORT INCLUDED A BROKEN CEILING AT 20,000 FEET, WITH 8 MILES OF VISIBILITY. THE TEMPERATURE WAS 69 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT AND THE DEW POINT WAS 53 DEGREES FAHRENHEIT.

(.19)ON APRIL 26, 2001, ABOUT 1435 EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME, AN AEROSPATIALE ATR 42-300, N223AT, REGISTERED TO GPA ATR II, INC., OPERATED BY AMERICAL EAGLE AIRLINES, AS FLIGHT 5238, ENCOUNTERED SEVERE TO MODERATE TURBULENCE DURING CRUISE FLIGHT OVER THE ATLANTIC OCEAN. INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED AT THE TIME AND AN INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES (IFR) FLIGHT PLAN WAS FILED FOR THE 14 CFR PART 121 SCHEDULED, INTERNATIONAL, PASSENGER FLIGHT. THE AIRPLANE WAS NOT DAMAGED AND THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE CAPTAIN, FIRST OFFICER, OR NINE PASSENGERS. THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT SUSTAINED SERIOUS INJURIES. THE FLIGHT ORIGINATED ABOUT 1355 FROM THE GEORGETOWN AIRPORT, GEORGETOWN, BAHAMAS. THE CAPTAIN REPORTED TO HIS COMPANY THAT THE FLIGHT WAS ENCOUNTERING LIGHT RAIN WHILE FLYING AT 16,000 FEET; THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT HAD THE SERVING CART OUT. THE WEATHER AVOIDANCE RADAR WAS NOT INDICATING ANY SERIOUS CONVECTIVE ACTIVITY AND THE CONTROLLER ADVISED THE FLIGHTCREW THAT HE WAS SHOWING TURBULENCE 20-30 MILES AHEAD. THE FLIGHT WAS VECTORED TO AVOID THE TURBULENCE AND ENCOUNTERED MODERATE TO SEVERE TURBULENCE AFTER ENTERING A CLOUD THAT WAS NOT SHOWING ON THE WEATHER RADAR. THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT REPORTEDLY BROKE BOTH LOWER BONES IN HER RIGHT LEG; SHE WAS ATTENDED BY A PASSENGER WHO IS AN EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN (EMT). THE FLIGHT CONTINUED TO THE DESTINATION AIRPORT AND LANDED UNEVENTFULLY. THE CAPTAIN FIRST DECLARED A MEDICAL EMERGENCY AT 1448 LOCAL, AND ADVISED THE CONTROLLER WHEN ASKED THAT THE FLIGHT HAD ENCOUNTERED TURBULENCE 50 MILES BACK. (-23) ON MAY 21, 2003, AT 2210 EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME, A SAAB 340B, N277MJ, OPERATED BY COLGAN AIRWARYS INC., AS FLI

(-23) ON MAY 21, 2003, AT 2210 EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME, A SAAB 340B, N277MJ, OPERATED BY COLGAN AIRWARYS INC., AS FLIGHT 5056, WAS SUBSTANTIALLY DAMAGED WHEN IT WAS STRUCK BY ANOTHER AIRPLANE, WHILE TAXIING AT LA GUARDIA AIRPORT (LGA), FLUSHING, NEW YORK. THE OTHER AIRPLANE, A DASSAULT DA-50, N664B, SUSTAINED MINOR DAMAGE. ONBOARD THE SAAB, THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT RECEIVED MINOR INJURIES, WHILE THE TWO PILOTS AND SIX PASSENGERS WERE NOT INJURED. ONBOARD THE DASSAULT, THE TWO PILOTS AND SEVEN PASSENGERS WERE ALSO NOT INJURED. NIGHT VISUAL METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS PREVAILED AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENT. THE SAAB WAS OPERATING AS A SCHEDULED PASSENGER FLIGHT CONDUCTED UNDER 14 CFR PART 121. THE DASSAULT WAS OPERATING AS BUSINESS FLIGHT CONDUCTED UNDER 14 CFR PART 91. ACCORDING TO THE PILOT-IN-COMMAND (PIC) OF THE DASSAULT, HIS AIRPLANE WAS PARKED AT THE "FIVE TOWERS" AREA, LOCATED ON THE WEST SIDE OF THE AIRPORT. AT 2205, THE PIC RECEIVED TAXI INSTRUCTIONS FROM THE GROUND CONTROLLER, WHICH THE PIC UNDERSTOOD AS, "MAKE TWO LEFT TURNS AND TAXI TO RUNWAY 13 FOR TAKEOFF VIA TAXIWAYS F AND BB." WHILE TAXIING NORTH ON TAXIWAY BB, THE DASSAULT COLLIDED WITH THE SAAB AT THE INTERSECTIONS OF BB ANDE. ACCORDING TO THE CAPTAIN OF THE SAAB, THE AIRPLANE WAS PUSHED OFF THE GATE TO SPOT 22, WHERE THE FIRST OFFICER THEN CALLED FOR TAXI CLEARANCE. THE TAXI INSTRUCTIONS WERE TO PROCEED "A SHORT OF K", FOR AN INBOUND BOEING 737. THE FLIGHT WAS THEN CLEARED FROM "A TO E, SHORT OF RUNWAY 4." THE FLIGHT RECEIVED FURTHER INSTRUCTIONS TO CROSS RUNWAY 04, AND TURN RIGHT AT "CC" TO TAXI TO RUNWAY 13. AFTER CROSSING RUNWAY 04, THE CAPTAIN NOTED A DASSAULT AIRPLANE TAXIING TO "BB", BUT HEARD HIS "HOLD SHORT" INSTRUCTIONS, AND CALLED FOR THE TAXI CHECKLIST. AS THE SAAB FLIGHTCREW WAS IN THE PROCESS OF COMPLETING THE TAXI CHECKLIST, THE DASSAULT STRUCK THEIR AIRPLANE FROM THE LEFT.

(-23) ON APRIL 12, 2007, AT APPROXIMATELY 0043 EDT, A BOMBARDIER CRJ-200 (N8905F), OPERATED BY PINNACLE AIRLINES AS

(-23) ON APRIL 12, 2007, AT APPROXIMATELY 0043 EDT, A BOMBARDIER CRJ-200 (N8905F), OPERATED BY PINNACLE AIRLINES AS FLIGHT 4712 FROM MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA TO TRAVERSE CITY, MICHIGAN, OVERRAN THE RUNWAY WHILE LANDING AT CHERRY CAPITAL AIRPORT, TRAVERSE CITY. THERE WERE NO INJURIES AMONG THE 49 PASSENGERS (INCLUDING 3 LAP-HELD INFANTS) AND 3 CREWMEMBERS AND THE AIRCRAFT RECEIVED SUBSTANTIAL DAMAGE. FLIGHT 4712 DEPARTED MINNEAPOLIS-ST. PAUL AIRPORT AT 2244 CENTRAL TIME. THE CREW REPORTED THE ENROUTE PORTION OF FLIGHT TO BE ROUTINE. AT APPROXIMATELY 0020 EASTERN TIME, THE FLIGHT WAS CLEARED FOR AN INSTRUMENT LANDING SYSTEM (ILS) APPROACH TO RUNWAY 28 BY MINNEAPOLIS AIR ROUTE TRAFFIC CONTROL CENTER. THE TRAVERSE CITY CONTROL TOWER HAD BEEN CLOSED SINCE AT 2200 PER NORMAL OPERATIONS. AUTOMATIC WEATHER OBSERVATION DATA INDICATED AT 2353 THE AIRPORT WAS EXPERIENCING LIGHT SNOW, WITH VISIBILITY OF ONE AND ONE HALF MILES, CLOUDS AT 900 AND 1500 FEET, AND WINDS FROM THE NORTH-NORTHEAST AT 7 KNOTS. AT 0030, THE VISIBILITY HAD DROPPED TO ONE-HALF MILE IN SNOW, WITH INDEFINITE CEILING AND VERTICAL VISIBILITY OF 400 FEET. SNOW REMOVAL OPERATIONS WERE IN PROGRESS AT THE AIRPORT, AND THE FLIGHT CREW COMMUNICATED DIRECTLY WITH AIRPORT OPERATIONS REGARDING THE RUNWAY CONDITIONS. AFTER LANDING, THE AIRPLANE OVERRAN THE DEPARTURE END OF RUNWAY 28. RUNWAY 28 IS 6,501 FEET LONG, WITH A PAVED BLAST PAD ABOUT 200 FEET LONG THE THRESHOLD. INITIAL EXAMINATION INDICATES THAT AS THE AIRPLANE EXITED THE PAVED SURFACE IT WAS ORIENTED ABOUT 600 DEGREES TO THE LEFT OF THE RUNWAY HEADING, AND ABOUT 30 FEET LEFT OF THE CENTERLINE. THE AIRPLANE ENTERED A GRASSY SNOW-COVERED FIELD BEYOND THE BLAST PAD AND THE NOSE GEAR SEPARATED APPROXIMATELY 93 FEET BEYOND THE END OF THE PAVEMENT. THE AIRPLANE SLEWED TO THE RIGHT AND CAME TO REST ORIENTED ABOUT 20 DEGREES LEFT OF CENTERLINE WITH THE RIGHT MAIN GEAR SUNKEN INTO THE GROUND AT A POINT ABOUT 100 FEET BEYOND THE PAVEMENT.

(-23) N633DL WAS DISCONNECTED FROM PUSHBACK FOR FLT. 1036 TPA-ATL, AFTER #1 ENGINE STARTED. THE CABIN WAS SECURED F

(-23) N633DL WAS DISCONNECTED FROM PUSHBACK FOR FLT. 1036 TPA-ATL, AFTER #1 ENGINE STARTED. THE CABIN WAS SECURED FOR DEPARTURE. DURING START OF #2 ENGINE, DEPARTING GROUND CREW OBSERVED SMOKE, FLAME, SMOKE AND FLAME FROM BACK OF ENGINE & GAVE COCKPIT CREW VISUAL HAND SIGNAL OF ENGINE FIRE. DURING THIS TIME, PASSENGERS IN THE RIGHT REAR TOURIST CABIN OBSERVED SMOKE AND FLAMES AND STARTED YELLING "FIRE", WHICH INITIATED A PANIC RUSH TO THE EXITS. A PASSENGER WAS OBSERVED TO GO TO THE L-2 DOOR, PUSH AND CURSE AT THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT AND OPENED THE L-2 DOOR, EVEN AFTER BEING TOLD BY THIS ATTENDANT NOT TO OPEN THE DOOR. THE PIC & F/O DID NOT OBSERVE ANY COCKPIT INDICATION OF A PROBLEM WITH THE #2 ENGINE - THE PIC SAID HE KNEW SOMETHING WAS WRONG WHEN HE OBSERVED A GROUND HANDLER WITH THEIR HANDS OVER THEIR FACE. HE THEN SHUTDOWN THE #2 ENGINE. THE PIC WAS CALLED BY THE R-1 FLIGHT ATTENDANT THAT THERE WAS A FIRE. THE COCKPIT CREW NOTED PASSENGERS ON THE RAMP & EMERGENCY/ENTRY DOOR LIGHTS WERE ON. THE PIC THEN SHUTDOWN THE #1 ENGINE. THE F/O CALLED GROUND CONTROL & REQUESTED EMERGENCY EQUIPMENT - FIRE TRUCKS & AMBULANCES. THE PIC MADE PA ANNOUNCEMENT TO STAY ON BOARD. 155 PAX. EVACUATED.(-23 1ST AMENDMENT) NOTE: THE FOLLOWING UPDATES MADE TO THIS BLOCK: 1) THIS INCIDENT WAS DECLARED AN ACCIDENT DUE TO SERIOUS INJURIES INVOLVED - 1 MALE WITH BROKEN WRIST. ANOTHER PAX. (-23) AT APPROXIMATELY 2105L, THURSDAY, MARCH 29, 2007 AN AIRTRAN AIRWAYS B-717-200 AIRCRAFT STRUCK A STATIONARY GALLEY SERVICE TRUCK DURING PUSHBACK FROM GATE D-1 AT ATLANTA'S HARTSFIELD-JACKSON INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT. NEITHER PILOT HAD KNOWLEDGE OF THE GALLEY SERVICE TRUCK DURING ANY PART OF THE PUSH-BACK OPERATION UNTIL THEY FELT A JOLT AND ADVISED THAT THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. THE PIC'S STATED THE AIRCRAFT WAS LOCATED ON GATE D1A, WHICH IS THE LABELING ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE JETWAY, BUT THE ACTUAL GATE IS D1 AS CORRECTLY LABELED IN THE TERMINAL BUILDING. WRITTEN STATEMENTS DESCRIBE THE PUSHBACK BEGINNING AND BOTH WING-WALKERS HAD REPOSITIONED THEMSELVES TO THE REAR AND ON EITHER SIDE OF THE AIRCRAFT TO CLEAR THE PATH ACROSS THE RAMP ROADWAY ACCORDING TO THEIR PROCEDURES. THE SERVICE TRUCK THEN ATTEMPTED TO DRIVE BETWEEN THIS AIRCRAFT AND AN AIRCRAFT PARKED AT THE NEIGHBORING GATE, D-1A. THE TUG DRIVER REPORTED OBSERVING THE WING-WALKER'S WARNING AND IMMEDIATELY APPLIED THE TUG BRAKES TO STOP BUT WITH UNSUFFICIENT TIME TO AVERT STRIKING THE LEFT AND REAR WING-TIP/POSITION LIGHT AREA. (-23) ON FRIDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2006, AT APPROXIMATELY 2201(L), B-1900D, N255GL, SCE FLIGHT #76, WITH 20 PASSENGERS (19 ADULTS AND 1 INFANT), WHILE LANDING AT KVGT, OVERRAN THE END OF RUNWAY 12R. THERE WERE NO INJURIES TO THE PASSENGERS AND CREW, BUT THERE WAS DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT PROPELLER AND TIRES, AND RUNWAY LIGHT. THE CHDO WAS NOT NOTIFIED UNTIL ON MONDAY, OCTOBER 9. SCE FLIGHT #76 WAS DISPATCHED FROM MERCED, CA (KMCE) TO KVGT AS AN IFR FLIGHT ON A DOMESTIC RELEASE. THE DO ASSERTS THAT THE FLIGHT WAS DISPATCHED PER FLIGHT OPERATIONS MANUAL AND DISPATCH PROCEDURES MANUAL STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURES. THE SIC WAS ALSO A LINE QUALIFIED BE-1900 PILOT-IN-COMMAND. THE DEPARTURE AND ENROUTE SEGMENTS OF THE FLIGHT WERE REPORTEDLY UNEVENTFUL. JUST BEFORE THE INCIDENT FLIGHT LANDED, THE ASOS REPORTED THE WINDS AS 180 DEG AT 5 KTS. THESE WINDS WERE WELL WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE B-1900D FOR RUNWAY 12R AND THE GIVEN AIRCRAFT CONFIGURATION AND WEIGHT, AND TEMPERATURE. THE SKY CONDITIONS WERE CLEAR AND THE VISIBILITY WAS 10+ SM. THE SIC STATES THAT AT APPROXIMATELY TWO MILES OUT ON FINAL APPROACH THE AIRCRAFT WAS SLIGHTLY HIGH AND AT VREF +15 KIAS. THE PIC WAS THE FLYING PILOT. THE SIC CALLED THIS DEVIATION OUT TO THE PIC AND THE PIC ACKNOWLEDGED, BUT THE PIC NEVER CORRECTED THE DEVIATION. AT SOME POINT BETWEEN SHORT-FINAL AND PASSING OVER THE THRESHOLD, THE PIC LOWERED THE NOSE SLIGHTLY TO GET BACK ON GLIDESLOPE, THUS MOST LIKELY INCREASING THE AIRSPEED SOMEWHAT. BOTH THE PIC AND SIC STATE THAT THE AIRCRAFT CROSSED THE THRESHOLD AT VREF +10. THE AIRCRAFT FLOATED, OR RATHER WAS ALLOWED TO FLOAT A CONSIDERABLE DISTANCE DOWN THE 5000' RUNWAY, APPROXIMATELY 1/2+ THE AVAILABLE RUNWAY LENGTH, TOUCHING DOWN APPROXIMATELY 2900 FEET FROM THE RWY APPROACH END AT TAXIWAY "H"; THIS WAS VERIFIED BY BOTH THE PIC AND SIC, AND TWO KVGT AIRPORT EMPLOYEES WHO WITNESSED THE LANDING. AT THIS POINT, THE REMAINING STOPPING DISTANCE AVAILABLE WAS APPROXIMATELY 2100 FEET. THE SIC STATES THAT AS THE AIRCRAFT FLOATED DOWN THE RUNWAY THAT HE ADVISED THE PIC THAT HE (PIC) WAS LONG, I.E., LANDING LONG. THE PIC ACKNOWLEDGED AND CONTINUED TO LAND THE AIRCRAFT. AT A POINT APPROXIMATELY 300 FEET FROM THE END OF THE RUNWAY, THE PIC ASKED FOR THE SIC TO HELP WITH THE BRAKING; THE SIC THEN ALSO APPLIED MAXIMUM BRAKING. THE AIRCRAFT IS NOT EQUIPPED WITH AN ANTI-SKID SYSTEM, THUS ALL FOUR MAIN WHEELS LOCKED UP AT SOME POINT. THE AIRCRAFT THEN BEGAN TO VEER OFF TO THE LEFT SLIGHTLY, EVENTUALLY STRAIGHTENING OUT, AND CONTINUING TO SLOW DOWN. THE AIRCRAFT EXITED THE END OF THE RUNWAY, ON THE LEFT SIDE, AND STOPPING APPROXIMATELY AN AIRCRAFT'S LENGTH ON THE HARD SURFACE OF THE OVERRUN AREA. AS THE AIRCRAFT PASSED THE END OF THE RUNWAY, THE LEFT PROPELLER AND LEFT MAIN GEAR CAME IN CONTACT WITH A RUNWAY-END IDENTIFIER LIGHT. THE LIGHT WAS DESTROYED AND TWO OF THE FOUR PROPELLER BLADES WERE DAMAGED. DURING THE MAXIMUM BRAKING, 3 OF THE 4 MAIN TIRES WERE FLAT-SPOTTED. THE LIGHT, PROPELLER, AND TIRES ALL NEEDED TO BE REPLACED. THE PIC THEN CONTINUED TO TAXI TO THE RAMP AND DEPLANE THE PASSENGERS. THE CREW HAD NOTICED THE FLAT-SPOTTED TIRES WHILE TAXIING TO THE RAMP AREA AND THE DAMAGE TO THE PROPELLER DURING THE POST-FLIGHT WALK-AROUND. THE PIC ENTERED THE MECHANICAL DISCREPANCIES IN THE AIRCRAFT LOGBOOK PER NORMAL COMPANY PROCEDURES, ADVISED THE DISPATCHER OF THE INCIDENT, AND THE PIC AND SIC SUBMITTED COMPANY AVIATION SAFETY REPORTS (ASRS). (-23) ON FEBRUARY 19, 2006, SKYWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT #20A (SKW20A) DEPARTED THE SALT LAKE CITY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT

(-23) ON FEBRUARY 19, 2006, SKYWEST AIRLINES FLIGHT #20A (SKW20A) DEPARTED THE SALT LAKE CITY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT ENROUTE TO GRAND JUNCTION, COLORADO. AFTER TAKEOFF SKW20A WAS CLEARED TO CLIMB TO FLIGHT LEVEL 210. DURING CLIMB OUT THE CREW RECEIVED A "L PACK HI PRESS" CAUTION MESSAGE AND CONSULTED THE QUICK REFERENCE HANDBOOK (QRH). THE QRH REQUIRED THEM TO REDUCE ENGINE POWER ON THE AFFECTED SIDE OF THE CAUTION MESSAGE RESULTING IN A REDUCED RATE OF CLIMB. ATC ISSUED AN EXPEDITED CLIMB DUE TO TERRAIN. SKW20A ADVISED UNABLE TO EXPEDITE CLIMB DUE TO PAC FAILURE. ATC ISSUED CLIMB TO 11,000 MSL AND AN IMMEDIATE LEFT TURN AWAY FROM TERRAIN. DUE TO REDUCED CLIMB PERFORMANCE AS A RESULT OF REDUCED POWER IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE QRH, SKW20A ENTERED 10,000 FOOT MINIMUM VECTORING ALTITUDE (MVA) AT 9600 FET AND A 10,400 FOOT MVA AT 9,900 FEET WHILE CLIMBING TO 11,000 FEET. WEATHER AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS DAY VFR. SKY20A WAS DISPATCHED WITH THE RIGHT AIR CONDITIONING PAC INOPERATIVE AND DIFFERED PER THE MINIMUM EQUIPMENT LIST (MEL). DURING TAKEOFF AND INITIAL CLIMB CONDITIONED AIR WAS BEING SUPPLIED TO THE AIRCRAFT CABIN BY THE AUXILIARY POWER UNIT (APU). AFTER TAKEOFF THE CONDITIONEDAIR WAS SWITCHED FROM THE APU SUPPLY TO ENGINES SUPPLY. WHEN CONDITION AIR WAS SWITCHED FROM APU TO ENGINES THE CREW FAILED TO FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE LISTED IN THE MEL BY CLOSING THE SUPPLY FROM THE APU AND ALLOWING PAC PRESSURE TO REDUCE TO LESS THEN 5 PSI BEFORE OPENING THE SUPPLY FROM THE ENGINES. AS A RESULT THE CREW RECEIVED A "L PACK HI PRESS" CAUTION MESSAGE REQUIRING THEM TO FOLLOW THE QHR PROCEDURES OF REDUCING ENGINE POWER. THIS REDUCTION IN ENGINE POWER PREVENTED THE AIRCRAFT FROM CLIMBING AT A RATE SUFFICIENT TO MEET AIRSPACE AND TERRAIN RESTRICTION. SKW20A NOTIFIED ATC OF THE PAC PROBLEM AND INFORMED THEM THEY WERE NOT ABLE TO EXPEDITE THEIR CLIMB, AS REQUESTED BY ATC, PRIOR TO PENETRATING AIRSPACE WHICH WAS BELOW THE MVA.

(-23) WHILE LANDING AT GCN, THE AIRCRAFT VEERED TO THE LEFT AND DEPARTED THE RUNWAY. THE AIRCRAFT THEN STRUCK A RUNWAY EDGE LIGHT WITH THE NOSE GEAR AND A FRANGIBLE TAXIWAY SIGN WITH THE RIGHT MAIN LANDING GEAR. WITNESSES WHO OBSERVED THE AIRCRAFT ON FINAL, STATED THAT THE NOSE GEAR APPEARED TO BE TURNED NEARLY 90 DEGREES TO THE DIRECTION OF FLIGHT. INSPECTION OF THE NOSE TIRE AT THE SCENE REVEALED CUPPING THAT APPEARED TO BE NEARLY 90 DEGREES TO THE DIRECTION OF LANDING. THE SWERVE MADE BY THE AIRCRAFT WAS HARD ENOUGH TO ROLL THE RIGHT MAIN TIRE OFF OF ITS RIM CAUSING IT TO DEFLATE. IT APPEARS THAT THIS INCIDENT WAS THE RESULT OF THREE INTERRELATED ISSUES. THE MAINTENANCE OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING CENTERING DEVICE AND INDICATOR; THE DESIGN OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM; AND INADEQUATE PILOT OPERATING PROCEDURES. AFTER RECOVERING THE AIRCRAFT, THE OPERATOR DISCOVERED THAT WITH THE COCKPIT NOSE WHEEL STEERING INDICATOR ALIGNED, THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING COLLAR DID NOT QUITE ALIGN WITH THE CENTERING TANG WHICH PREVENTED THE NOSE WHEEL FROM LOCKING IN THE CENTERED POSITION WHILE AIRBORNE. WHILE IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT THE CLEARANCES IN THE SYSTEM WERE WITHIN TOLERANCE, WHEN COMBINED,IN THIS CASE, THEY APPARENTLY PREVENTED THE NOSE WHEEL FROM BEING LOCKED IN THE CENTERED POSITION. THE OPERATOR HAS REVISED THEIR INSPECTION AND MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES IN AN EFFORT TO MAINTAIN TIGHTER TOLERANCES WITHIN THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM. REGARDING DESIGN OF THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING SYSTEM, THE HANDLE IS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE YOKE AND APPEARS CAPABLE OF BEING ACCIDENTALLY BUMPED. THIS WOULD CAUSE AN UNLATCHED NOSE WHEEL TO MOVE FROM A CENTERED POSITION AS ON THE INCIDENT AIRCRAFT. FINALLY, THE OPERATOR LACKED A PROCEDURE THAT WOULD ENSURE THAT THE NOSE WHEEL WAS, IN FACT, CENTERED AND LATCHED. THIS INCIDENT HAS BEEN RESOLVED BY THE PUBLICATION OF A NEW PILOT PROCEDURE TO BE ACCOMPLISHED BOTH AFTER TAKE-OFF AND BEFORE LANDING. THE PROCEDURE IS TO MOVE THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING LEVER UP AND DOWN IN ORDER TO FEEL THAT THE NOSE GEAR HAD MECHANICALLY LOCKED INTO THE CENTER POSITION.

CREW THEN CONTINUED TO DECELERATE AS THEY ROLLED THE NEXT 4000 FEET TOWARD THE FAR END OF THE RUNWAY. THE CAPTAIN APPLIED THE BRAKES AGAIN AT ABOUT 15 KNOTS AT APPROXIMATELY 800 FEET FROM THE END OF THE RUNWAY. INITIALLY, CAPTAIN STATED THAT BRAKING FELT NORMAL FOR THE SNOWY CONDITIONS, WITH SOME ANTI-SKID CYCLING. AS CAPTAIN APPLIED THE BRAKES HARDER FOR THE TURN-OFF, AIRCRAFT STARTED A CONTINUOUS SKID FROM APPROXIMATELY 10 KNOTS TO ZERO. CAPTAIN FURTHER STATED HE "STOOD" ON THE BRAKES, TRYING TO STOP THE AIRCRAFT AS THEY SLOWLY SKIDDED STRAIGHT AHEAD. AIRCRAFT EVENTUALLY CAME TO A STOP AT THE CENTERLINE WITH THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT JUST SHORT OF THE RUNWAY END AND FIRST ROW OF LIGHTS. CREW WAS UNABLE AT THIS POINT TO MAKE A SAFE 90 DEGREE TURN FROM THAT POSITION TO EXIT THE RUNWAY. DUE TO THE "NIL" BRAKING CONDITIONS AND HOW CLOSE THE CREW WAS TO THE END OF THE RUNWAY, CAPTAIN CHOSE NOT TO MOVE THE AIRCRAFT ANY FURTHER UNDER POWER. CREW THEN ELECTED TO SHUT DOWN BOTH ENGINES, AND DISABLE THE AIRCRAFT ON THE RUNWAY DUE TO THE SLICK CONDITIONS. AT THIS POINT, CAPTAIN COORDINATED WITH ATC, DISPATCH, AND OPERATIONS TO HAVE THE AIRCRAFT TOWED TO THE GATE BY SWAA PERSONNEL. UNFORTUNATELY, THE TUG DRIVER KNOCKED OVER A RUNWAY LIGHT WHILE MANEUVERING TO HOOK UP THE TOW BAR. AFTER SOME REPOSITIONING OF THE TUG, AND ASSISTANCE FROM SNOWPLOW OPERATORS THE AIRCRAFT WAS FINALLY TOWED TO THE GATE WITHOUT FURTHER DIFFICULTY. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED BY THE PASSENGERS OR CREW MEMBERS. SWAA GROUND OPERATIONS ARRIVED AT THE END OF THE RUNWAY AND ATTEMPTED TO TOW THE AIRCRAFT TO THE GATE. APPROXIMATELY ONE HOUR LATER SWAA OPERATIONS WERE THEN ABLE TO TOW THE AIRCRAFT TO THE GATE WITHOUT FURTHER INCIDENT. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. AFTER SWAA MANAGEMENT SPOKE WITH AIRPORT MANAGER ^PRIVACY DATA^, IT WAS DETERMINED THE COMMUNICATION BETWEEN THE AIRPORT SNOW REMOVAL TEAMS FROM ONE SHIFT TO ANOTHER WAS NOT WHAT IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN DURING THE EVENT. HOWEVER, DUE TO FLIGHT ACTIVITY AND SHIFT CHANGE THE RUNWAY WAS NOT PLOWED FROM 19:00 UNTIL AFTER FLIGHT 522 LANDED AT 19:54. ^PRIVACY DATA^ REASSURED SWAA THAT THE NEW PROCEDURES FOR "SHIFT CHANGES" DURING A WEATHER EVENT WILL PREVENT THE SAME SCENARIO FROM HAPPENING AGAIN. BASICALLY, NEW SNOW REMOVAL PROCEDURES WILL REQUIRE THE SNOW REMOVAL CREWS TO CONTINUE THEIR SHIFT UNTIL THE CREW COMING ON IS IN PLACE AND READY TO TAKE OVER THE SNOW REMOVAL PROCESS.

(-23) ON MAY 18, 2007, AT 1320 EST, A NORTHWEST AIRLINES, DC-9-31, FLIGHT 1411, N1799U EXPERIENCED A CABIN PRESSURIZATION PROBLEM DURING CLIMB AFTER DEPARTING FROM SYRACUSE HANCOCK INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, SYRACUSE, NY (SYR) TO DETROIT, MI. ACCORDING TO THE FAA CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT OFFICE FOR NORTHWEST AIRLINES THE AIRPLANE WAS CLIMBING THROUGH 19,000 FEET MSL AFTER DEPARTURE FROM SYR WHEN THE FLIGHT CREW HEARD A "LOUD POP" AND THE CABIN DEPRESSURIZED. THE FLIGHT CREW INITIATED AN EMERGENCY DESCENT TO 10,000 FEET. AFTER REACHING 10,000 FEET THE FLIGHT CREW DIVERTED INTO THE BUFFALO-NIAGARA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT, BUFFALO, NY (BUF). AFTER THE AIRCRAFT LANDED IT WAS INSPECTED BY THE ARFF, IT WAS RELEASED TO CONTINUED TAXI TO THE GATE. UPON FURTHER INSPECTION A CREASE IN THE SKIN OF THE FUSELAGE FORWARD OF THE TEAR INDICATING THE SKIN BEING DAMAGED BY A FOREIGN OBJECT. COMPANY MAINTENANCE FLEW INTO BUF AND PUT A TEMPORARY REPAIR ON THE FUSELAGE SKIN IN ORDER TO FERRY TO A MAINTENANCE FACILITY FOR A PERMANENT REPAIR. A TELEPHONE CONVERSATION WITH THE SYR NOTHWEST AIRLINES STATION MANAGER (SM) REVEALED THE FOLLOWING: ON MAY 18, 2007, THE SM STATED THAT HE WAS IN A MEETING WHEN HE HEARD ABOUT FLIGHT 1411 DIVERTING INTO BUF DUE TO A PRESSURIZATION PROBLEM AROUND 1 PM. HE THEN PROCEEDED TO CONTACT THE CONTRACT RAMP PERSONNEL WHO WORKED THE FLIGHT. THERE WERE TWO, ONE A TUG DRIVER AND ANOTHER THAT ASSISTED. THE BELT LOADER WAS PARKED BY THE FORWARD CARGO BIN AND UPON THE COMPLETION OF ON LOADING PASSENGER BAGS THEY TRIED TO START THE BELT LOADER, BUT IT DIED. IN ORDER TO MOVE THE BELT LOADER ONE OF THE RAMP PERSONNEL GOT THE TUG AND POSITIONED THE TUG BETWEEN THE AIRCRAFT AND THE BELT LOADER. THE DRIVER WAS ABLE TO GET THE BELT LOADER OUT OF THE WAY FOR THE AIRCRAFT TO DEPART. THE DRIVER OF THE TUG TOLD THE SM HE HAD NO IDEA ABOUT A SKIN TEAR. THE SM SAID HE INSPECTED THE TUG, AND DISCOVERED THAT "THE PAINT ON THE ROOF OF THE TUG MATCHED THE PAINT OF THE AIRCRAFT WHERE THE SKIN TEAR OCCURRED." HE BROUGHT THIS TO THE ATTENTION OF THE TUG DRIVER AND THE OTHER RAMP PERSON, BUT THEY BOTH DENIED ANY SORT OF DAMAGE OR SEEING A TEAR OF THE FUSELAGE SKIN. THE SM CONTACTED TEH AIR WISCONSIN MANAGER (RAMP CONTRACTOR) TO INFORM HIM ABOUT THE GROUND INCIDENT WITH TWO OF HIS EMPLOYEES. THEY WERE BOTH REMOVED IMMEDIATELY FROM THEIR DUTIES, AND AFTER FURTHER INVESTIGATION FIRED FROM AIR WISCONSIN. THE AIRCRAFT SKIN TEAR WAS REPAIRED WITHIN A FEW DAYS AND THE AIRCRAFT RETURNED BACK TO SERVICE.

VISUAL WEATHER CONDITIONS PREVAILED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT, AND FLIGHT 1579 OPERATED ON AN INSTRUMENT FLIGHT RULES FLIGHT PLAN. (-23) DURING A FLIGHT FROM OPA LOCKA, FL TO CINCINNATI, OH, WHILE IN THE VICINITY OF VERO BEACH, FL, THE FLIGHT CRE

(-23) DURING A FLIGHT FROM OPA LOCKA, FL TO CINCINNATI, OH, WHILE IN THE VICINITY OF VERO BEACH, FL, THE FLIGHT CREW OF N41527, A CV-440 OPERATED BY MIAMI AIR LEASE, NOTICED OIL PRESSURE AND OIL TEMPERATURE PROBLEMS WITH THE RIGHT ENGINE, FOLLOWED BY SIGNIFICANT ENGINE VIBRATION. THE CREW ELECTED TO SHUT DOWN AND FEATHER THE RIGHT ENGINE, AND PLANNED AN EMERGENCY LANDING AT VERO BEACH MUNICIPAL AIRPORT. WHILE APPROACHING THE LEFT DOWNWIND FOR RUNWAY 11 AT VRB, THE AIRCRAFT'S ELECTRICAL SYSTEM FAILED. THE CREW PERFORMED AN EMERGENCY EXTENSION OF THE LANDING GEAR, BUT UPON TOUCHDOWN, EXPERIENCED NO HYDRAULIC BRAKING OR STEERING. EMERGENCY BRAKING USING THE AIRCRAFT'S AIR SYSTEM WAS ACCOMPLISHED. THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY APPROXIMATELY 500 FEET FROM THE END OF RUNWAY 11, AND CAME TO REST ADJACENT TO THE END OF THE RUNWAY APPROXIMATELY 100 FEET FROM THE RIGHT SIDE OF THE RUNWAY. THE RIGHT MAIN BRAKE CAUGHT FIRE DUE TO HEAT CAUSED BY HEAVY BRAKING. THE CREW EXITED THE AIRCRAFT AND ATTEMPTED TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE USING HAND HELD FIRE EXTINGUISHERS. THIS ATTEMPT WAS UNSUCCESSFUL, AND THE FIRE WAS FINALLY EXTINGUISHED BY THE VRB AIRPORT FIRE DEPARTMENT. THE FLIGHTCREW WAS NOT INJURED, AND THE AIRCRAFT SUSTAINED MINOR FIRE DAMAGE. A POST INCIDENT INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE CREW FAILED TO "UNLOAD" THE ELECTRICAL SYSTEM FOLLOWING THE SHUT DOWN OF THE RIGHT ENGINE, SUBSEQUENTLY CAUSING OVERLOAD AND FAILURE OF THE MAIN CURRENT LIMITER. ADDITIONALLY, THE CREW APPARENTLY FAILED TO PLACE THE HYDRAULIC BY-PASS VALVE IN THE "DOWN" (NOT BY-PASSED) POSITION, THUS PREVENTING THE LANDING GEAR FROM EXTENDING NORMALLY. THE CAUSE OF SUBSEQUENT FAILURES OF THE HYDRAULIC STEERING THE BRAKING SYSTEM WERE NOT POSITIVELY DETERMINED. HOWEVER, FAILURE OF THE FLIGHT CREW TO FOLLOW APPROPRIATE EMERGENCY CHECK LIST PROCEDURES FOLLOWING SHUT DOWN OF THE RIGHT ENGINE RESULTED IN SIGNIFICANT COMPLICATIONS DURING THE EMERGENCY LANDING, AND SUBSEQUENT DAMAGE TO THE AIRCRAFT. ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ ADDITIONALLY, INSPECTION OF N41527 REVEALED SEVERAL POTENTIAL AIRWORTHINESS ISSUES ASSOCIATED WITH THE AIRCRAFT. FURTHER INVESTIGATION BY THE PRINCIPAL AIRWORTHINESS INSPECTOR ASSIGNED TO MIAMI AIR LEASE IS RECOMMENDED.

(-23) ON JULY 8, 2003, AT 12:30 CENTRAL STANDARD TIME, AN AMERICAN AIRLINES F-100 AIRCRAFT, N1414D, WAS PARKED AT GATE H-12 AT O'HARE INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT IN CHICAGO, ILLINOIS WHEN A BAGGAGE CART STRUCK IT. AN INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE CART WAS BEING TOWED BY AMERICAN AIRLINES TUG #17604 AND BECAME DETACHED FROM THE TOW HOOK WHILE THE TUG WAS IN MOTION. THE DRIVER TURNED THE TUG AWAY FROM THE WING AND THE DETACHED CART CONTINUED STRAIGHT, IMPACTING THE LEFT WING AND BECOMING STUCK. PASSENGERS HAD ALREADY CLEARED THE AIRCRAFT, BUT FOUR CREWMEMBERS WERE STILL ON BOARD AT THE TIME OF IMPACT. THERE WERE NO INJURIES ON THE GROUND OR IN THE AIRCRAFT. THE DRIVER OF THE TUG RECEIVED A CITATION FOR CARELESS DRIVING FROM THE CHICAGO POLICE. AMERICAN AIRLINES ALSO DETERMINED THAT THE INDIVIDUAL HAD FAILED TO PROPERLY SECURE THE CART TO THE TUG. AMERICAN AIRLINES MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL EXTRACTED THE CART FROM THE WING AND DISCOVERED THAT THE CART HAD PUNCTURED THE WING FUEL TANK AND CREATED A MINOR FUEL SPILL. THE CHICAGO POLICE SECURED THE AREA AND A SPILL TEAM WAS DISPATCHED FOR A CLEANUP. AMERICAN AIRLINES MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL TRANSFERRED FUEL OUT OF THE TANK AND TAXIED THE AIRCRAFT TO THE HANGER FOR EVALUATION. MAINTENANCE AND ENGINEERING PERSONNEL EVALUATED THE DAMAGE THAT INCLUDED THE PUNCTURE IN THE INBOARD LEFT WING FUEL TANK ACCESS PANEL, DEEP SCRAPES TO THE OUTBOARD ACCESS PANEL AND SCRAPES ON THE LOWER SURFACE OF THE WING. ENGINEERING PERSONNEL AT AMERICAN AIRLINES TULSA MAINTENANCE FACILITY DETERMINED THAT THE DAMAGE WAS TOO EXTENSIVE TO BE REPAIRED AT O'HARE. TEMPORARY REPAIRS WERE MADE AT O'HARE AND A FERRY PERMIT WAS ISSUED FOR A ONE-TIME FLIGHT TO TULSA FOR REPAIRS.

(-23) MIAMI AIR LEASE WHICH OPERATES A CONVAIR 340, TAIL NUMBER N41626 SERIAL NUMBER 274, DEPARTED OPF AT 0840 THIS MORNING, HEADING TO NASSAU, BAHAMAS ISLANDS. WHILE CLIMBING AND PERFORMING THE AFTER TAKE OFF CHECKLIST, THE CREW NOTICED A VIBRATION. THEY CHECKED THEIR INDICATION AND SAW NOTHING IRREGULAR. THE PILOT STATES THAT HE LOOKED OUT OF THE LEFT SIDE WINDOW AND AT THAT TIME SAW WHITE SMOKE AS WELL AS OIL. HE INITIATED THE EMERGENCY CHECKLIST AND SHUTDOWN THE ENGINE. HOWEVER, THE #1 ENGINE FAILED TO FEATHER. THEY NOTIFIED MIAMI APPROACH AND STATED THAT THEY WERE RETURNING TO OPF. AT THAT TIME THEY HAD NOT DECLARED AN EMERGENCY. AFTER PUSHING #2 ENGINE TO MAX POWER, THEY DETERMINED THAT DUE TO THE DRAG FROM THE #1 ENGINE NOT BEING FEATHERED AND DUE TO THE MAX LOAD OF CARGO, THEY WERE UNABLE TO MAINTAIN ALTITUDE. THEY THEN CONTACTED TOWER AND DECLARED AN EMERGENCY. THEY TURNED INTO THE GOOD ENGINE AND PROCEEDED TO FIND A LOCATION TO DITCH. UPON CROSSING OVER US 1, THEY CLEARED SOME HIGH TENSION WIRES, AND DITCHED INTO MAUL LAKE. ON THEIR DESCENT THE AIRCRAFT DID CONTACT SOME TREES BUT ONLY SCRAPED THE BOTTOM OF THE AIRCRAFT. THE AIRCRAFT LAYS IN APPROXIMATELY 10-12 FEET OF WATER.                                                                        (-23 AMENDMENT) NTSB HAS STARTED THE INSPECTION OF THE PROP AND ENG. FIRST TASK ACCOMPLISHED WAS TO APPLY POWER TO THE FEATHER PUMP TO ATTEMPT TO FEATHER THE PROP. TWO OF THE THREE BLADES WERE APPROXIMATELY 30 DEGREES INTO FEATHER WHILE THE LAST BLADE WAS ABOUT 3 DEGREES INTO THE FEATHER. UPON APPLYING POWER THE BLADES DID NOT MOVE, AFTER ADJUSTING THE PRESSURE THE BLADES MOVED ABOUT 5 DEGREES. THE PROP GOVERNOR HOUSING BEGAN TO LEAK OIL. THE PROP WAS REMOVED AND NO VISIBLE DAMAGE COULD BE SEEN. THE GOVERNOR WAS REMOVED, BUT WE WERE UNABLE TO VERIFY IF THE TEFLON SEAL WAS OF THE CORRECT PART NUMBER. SPECULATION IS THAT THE LEAK COULD HAVE BEEN CAUSED BY POST CRASH IMPACT AND OR WATER CONTAMINATION FROM SITTING IN THE LAKE. THE PROPS AS WELL AS THE PROP GOVERNOR WAS TAKEN INTO CUSTODY BY ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ OF AERO PROPELLER OF MIAMI INC, FOR TEAR DOWN PER REQUEST OF THE NTSB. THE RESULTS OF THE TEARDOWN WILL BE AVAILABLE ON DECEMBER 22, 2004. FURTHER TEARDOWN OF THE ENG FRONT CASE REVEALED SEVERE DAMAGE. THE OIL SCAVENGE PUMP DRIVE SHAFT WAS SHEARED OFF AND THE PUMP WAS FROZEN. THE MAIN OIL PUMP PLATE MOUNT BOLTS WERE SHEARED OFF. THE MAIN OIL PUMP GEARS WERE SHEARED OFF. A LARGE AMOUNT OF METAL WAS FOUND IN THE BOTTOM OF THE CASE. FURTHER TEARDOWN IS REQUIRED, AS THE MAIN BREAK DOWN SEEMS TO BE FURTHER DOWN INSIDE OF THE ENGINE. MOST OF THE CARGO WAS RECOVERED FROM THE ACFT. ALTHOUGH SATURATED WITH WATER, THE NTSB REQUESTED THAT WE WEIGH IT FOR A BALLPARK FIGURE. THIS WAS ACCOMPLISHED. TELEPHONE CONVERSATION WITH ^PRIVACY DATA OMITTED^ REGARDING THE PROPELLER. HE STATED THAT ALL THE SWITCHES AS WILL AS THE GOVERNOR CHECKED OUT. THE MAIN CAUSE OF THE PROP NOT FEATHERING WAS DUE TO THE OIL TRANSFER TUBE HAD BROKEN IN HALF THUS THE OIL WAS DUMPING INTO THE HOUSING AND NOT PRESSURIZING THE GOVERNOR, THUS THE PROP W/N FEATHER. AS TO THE ENGINE, THE NTSB HAS DECIDED NOT TO CONTINUE ON WITH THE TEARDOWN. THE FINDINGS SEEM TO LEAD TO THE MASTER ROD BEARING FAILED AS THE PRIMARY MALFUNCTION THAT LED TO THE OTHER ASSOCIATED DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE. THE PRELIMINARY PROGNOSES ARE LEANING TOWARDS IMPROPER MAINTENANCE STORAGE PROCEDURES.

WHEN INSPECTOR RAUPP, OLIVER AND HILL ARRIVED ON THE SCENE THE PIC TERRY BURLINGAME (201427826) AND F/O JOHN CATURIA (474605767) WERE NOT AT THE AIRCRAFT. AFTER COMPLETING OUR AIRCRAFT INSPECTION WE OBSERVED TIRE DEBRIS AND TWO SETS OF TIRE SKID MARKS ALIGNED WITH THE AIRCRAFT AT M-3 AND "F" TAXIWAY MARKERS. INSPECTOR RAUPP CONTACTED ROBERT TALMADGE POI FOR AALA TO REQUEST CREW HISTORY AND CAPTAINS REPORT AND ALL AVAILABLE INFORMATION CONCERNING THIS INCIDENT. THE INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM AALA WAS RECEIVED ON 15 APRIL 2002 ALONG WITH AN OPERATIONAL SYNOPSIS FROM AALA T.J. AHERN VICE PRESIDENT SAFETY, SECURITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL WHICH STATED FLIGHT 1949 DEPARTED MSP WITH THE ANTI-SKID PLACARDED INOPERATIVE. THE CAPTAIN WAS FLYING. THE FLIGHT LANDED AT ORD ON RUNWAY 09R. (-23) ON THURSDAY OCTOBER 2, 2003 AT 06:15 LOCAL TIME, A CANADAIR CL-600-2B19 AIRCRAFT, BEARING REGISTRATION NUMBER N959CA, OPERATING UNDER 14 CFR PART 121 AS COMAIR FLIGHT 5319, DEPARTED THE GREATER ROCHESTER INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (ROC) IN ROCHESTER, NY. ACCORDING TO THE FLIGHT CREW, AS THEY RETRACTED THE LANDING GEAR, A LANDING GEAR DISAGREE CAUTION LIGHT ILLUMINATED. THE CREW COMPLETED THE EMERGENCY PROCEDURE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE QUICK REFERENCE HANDBOOK, EXTENDED THE LANDING GEAR, DECLARED AN EMERGENCY WITH THE ROCHESTER AIRPORT TRAFFIC CONTROL TOWER. THE AIRCRAFT LANDED SAFELY ON RUNWAY 22 AT ROC. SHORTLY AFTER INITIATING A TAXI, THE CREW NOTED THAT THE NOSE WHEEL STEERING WAS INOPERATIVE. THE CREW STOPPED THE AIRCRAFT, NOTIFIED ATC AND SHUT DOWN THE ENGINES. AIRPORT SHUTTLE BUSSES WERE USED TO RETURN PASSENGERS TO THE TERMINAL. A TUG WAS USED TO TOW THE AIRCRAFT TO THE RAMP. A LOCAL CONTRACT MAINTENANCE PROVIDER DETERMINED THAT THE TORQUE LINK WAS IMPROPERLY CONNECTED BEFORE THE AIRCRAFT HAD TAXIED FROM THE GATE. ACCORDING TO THE MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN, WEAR AND DAMAGE SIGNATURES PRESENT ON THE TORQUE LINK INDICATE THAT THE BUSHING (LOCATED ON THE LOWER TORQUE LINK), WAS RESTING ON-TOP-OF THE LOCKING PINS (LOCATED ON THE UPPER TORQUE LINK), AS OPPOSED OT THE PROPER CONDITION IN WHICH THE PINS PASS THROUGH THE BUSHING. THIS CONDITION PROVIDED THE AIRCRAFT WITH ENOUGH STABILITY TO GIVE THE CREW STEERING (DIRECTIONAL CONTROL) DURING THE TAXI TO THE RUNWAY. ACCORDING TO THE MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN, DAMAGE SIGNATURES INDICATE THAT UPON LANDING, THE LOWER TORQUE LINK JAMMED TO THE LEFT OF THE UPPER TORQUE LINK AND THE RIGHT SIDE LOCKING PIN. (-23) ON MAY 29, 2002, AT APPROXIMATELY 0900 LOCAL, UNITED AIRLINES A-320 AIRCRAFT, N435UA, FLIGHT 1676, ORD TO TPA EXPERIENCED A NUMBER 2 ENGINE SHUTDOWN IN FLIGHT JUST BELOW 3000FT AFTER TAKEOFF ON CLIMB OUT. THE CREW REPORTED THAT AT ABOUT 2000 FEET, EGT AND EPR BEGAN TO RISE. AT ABOUT 3000 FEET THERE WAS A LOUD BANG WITH AN OVER HEAT AND ENGINE 2 FAIL MESSAGE. THE SHUT DOWN AND FIRE PROCEDURES WERE THEN COMPLETED AND THE FLIGHT RETURNED TO ORD WITH NO FUEL BEING DUMPED AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS NOT OVERWEIGHT ON LANDING . THERE WERE 67 PASSENGERS ON BOARD WITH A COCKPIT CREW OF 2 AND A CABIN CREW OF 3. THE AIRCRAFT TAXIED TO THE GATE AND PASSENGERS WERE DEPLANED NORMALLY. THE CREW USED ONE FIRE BOTTLE IN FLIGHT AND DURING THE TAXI THEY USED THE ALTERNATE BOTTLE. AT THE GATE, A TECHNICIAN (MECHANIC) USED ANOTHER FIRE EXTINGUISHER TO SPRAY THE TURBINE/TAILPIPE AREA, AND AN AIRPORT FIRE TRUCK THEN SPRAYED THE INTAKE AND ENTIRE ENGINE AREA. A PRELIMINARY INSPECTION OF THE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE WAS CONDUCTED AT THE TERMINAL GATE AND IT WAS NOTED THAT THE LP TURBINE MODULE WAS DESTROYED DUE TO AN INTERNAL FIRE. ALL TURBINE COMPONENTS REMAINED WITHIN THE ENGINE CASE, HOWEVER THIS FAILURE WAS CONTAINED SINCE THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF THE FIRE SPREADING OUT OF THE ENGINE CASE. THERE WAS EVIDENCE OF MODERATE HEAT RADIATION DAMAGE SPREADING TO THE INTERNAL ENGINE COWLING, THRUST REVERSERS, PYLON FAIRING PANELS, ENGINE MOUNTS AND OTHER EXTERNAL ENGINE COMPONENTS. UNITED AIRLINES SFO ENGINEERING REVEALED THAT THIS V-2500 ENGINE, SERIAL NUMBER V10390 WAS A HIGH TIME ENGINE WITH 12,780 HOURS, 4380 CYCLES AND WAS THE ORIGINAL ENGINE THAT WAS DELIVERED WITH THE AIRCRAFT. SEVERAL COMPONENTS IN THE FUEL/BLEED VALVE SYSTEM WERE REPLACED, AIRCRAFT/ENGINES RUN NUMEROUS TIMES AT POWER, AND THE ORIGINAL PROBLEM FIXED. TROUBLESHOOTING OF THOSE PROBLEMS WAS DONE IN COORDINATION WITH SFO ENGINEERING AND DEFECTIVE COMPONENTS WERE CONFIRMED, UNITED AIRLINES ENGINEERING AND MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL WERE SATISFIED THAT THEY HAD FIXED THE PROBLEM BEFORE RELEASING THE AIRCRAFT AS SERVICEABLE BEFORE IT'S DEPARTURE ON FLIGHT 1676 ON MAY 29. THE AIRCRAFT WAS SUBSEQUENTLY TOWED TO THE MAINTENANCE HANGER WHERE THE ENGINE WAS REPLACED. THE PYLON STRUCTURE, ENGINE MOUNTS AND PYLON FAIRING PANELS WERE INSPECTED FOR HEAT DAMAGE AND WERE EITHER REPAIRED OR REPLACED AND IN SOME CASE TESTED OK. NOTE: INCIDENT PHOTOGRAPHS ARE IN THE CUSTODY OF THE REPORTING INSPECTOR.

(-23) ON APRIL 1, 2003, AIRCRAFT N175UA, OPERATING AS UA FLT 896-1 HKG TO ORD DECLARED AN EMERGENCY ON DESCENT AND APPROACH INTO ORD DUE TO A RESTRICTION IN THE ABILITY TO ROLL THE AIRPLANE TO THE LEFT WITH THE CONTROL WHEE. THE CREW WAS CLEARED FOR A LONG STRAIGHT IN APPROACH TO RUNWAY 14R AND HAD AN UNEVENTFUL LANDING AND ROLLOUT. AFTER TAXIING INTO THE GATE, THE CREW WAS ABLE TO OPERATE THE CONTROL WHEEL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS WITH NO RESTRICTIONS. ABOUT 4 HOURS OUTSIDE OF ORD THEY NOTED THAT THEIR PORTABLE WATER TANKS WERE EMPTY AND THAT WATER WAS DRAINING INTO THE PASSENGER CABIN FROM THE CEILING ALONG THE RIGHT HAND AISLE, BETWEEN DOORS 2R AND 3R. UPON PARKING AT THE GATE, THE AIRCRAFT HAD A SIGNIFICANT AMOUNT OF WATER DRAINING FROM THE FUSELAGE DRAIN MASTS AND THE MAIN DECK FLOOR BETWEEN DOOR 2R AND 3R WAS COMPLETELY SATURATED. THE UPPER DECK CART LIFT SHAFT HAD WATER ALONG THE BASE ON THE MAIN DECK. ONCE THE AIRCRAFT ARRIVED IN THE HANGAR, THE TROUBLESHOOTING PLAN FOCUSED ON THE POSSIBILITY THAT THE AILERON CONTROL EVENT AND THE WATER DRAINAGE ISSUE COULD BE RELATED. IT WAS THEORIZED THAT THIS COULD HAVE BEEN THE RESULT OF WATER FREEZING ON THE AILERON CONTROL CABLES IN THE MAIN LANDING GEAR WHEEL WELL, BASED ON SIMILAR IN-FLIGHT EVENTS FROM OTHER OPERATORS AS PER BOEING SERVICE BULLETIN 747-51A2057, INSPECTION OF THE "CANTED PRESSURE DECK DRAINAGE SYSTEM." DURING THE ISOLATION AND TROUBLESHOOTING OF A POSSIBLE WATER LEAK IN THE PASSENGER CABIN AREA AND THE UPPER DECK GALLEY, THE FOLLOWING CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE P414 PANEL IN THE E&E (ELECTRICAL/ELECTRONIC COMPARTMENT) WERE FOUND OPEN AND NOT TAGGED: 1. 414L22 FWD DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 2. 414L23 CENTER DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 3. 414L24 AFT DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR MODE 4. 414C21 DRAIN MAST HEATER GROUND MODE THE ABOVE NOTED CIRCUIT BREAKERS WERE PULLED AS PART OF A MAINTENANCE TASK TO SUPPORT THE CLEANING OF THE OVERBOARD DRAIN LINES TO THE AIRCRAFT EXTERIOR DRAIN MAST. THIS WAS ACCOMPLISHED AT HKG (HONG KONG) ON MARCH 31, 2003. DURING THE SUBSEQUENT TROUBLESHOOTING BY MAINTENANCE AND ENGINEERING IT WAS NOTED THAT WHEN THE DRAIN MASTS WERE PLUGGED (SIMULATING A FROZEN CONDITION), WATER BACKED UP THROUGH THE UPPER DECK GALLEY CHILLER DRAIN AND BEGAN TO OVERFLOW INTO THE CABIN THROUGH THE CEILING PANELS ALONG THE RIGHT HAND AISLE IN BUSINESS CLASS. (-23) ON AUGUST 16, 2002 THE O'HARE FLIGHT STANDARDS DISTRICT OFFICE RECEIVED A NOTICE FROM THE GREAT LAKES REGIONAL CONTROL CENTER THAT UNITED AIRLINES FLIGHT 1133, A B-737, ENROUTE AND DESCENDING INTO ORD, REPORTED AN UNCOMMANDED ROLL EVENT. AN INVESTIGATION INTO THIS INCIDENT WAS CONDUCTED AND THE FOLLOWING NARRATIVE CONTAINS THE FACTS OF THIS EVENT: WHILE THE AIRCRAFT WAS DESCENDING, DOWNWIND OF ORD RUNWAY 4 RIGHT, AND NOT FOLLOWING ANY HEAVY AIRCRAFT, WITH NO TURBULENCE THROUGH 7000 FEET AT 250KTS, A SLIGHT AIRFRAME RUMBLE WAS HEARD FOLLOWED BY THE RIGHT RUDDER PEDAL MOVING SLIGHTLY FORWARD. THE "A" AUTO PILOT WAS ENGAGED AT THAT TIME. THE AIRCRAFT THEN BEGAN TO GRADUALLY ROLL TO THE LEFT, AT WHICH TIME THE CAPTAIN DISCONNECTED THE AUTO PILOT AT 15 DEGREES LEFT ROLL. THE AIRCRAFT CONTINUED TO ROLL LEFT 20 TO 25 DEGREES BEFORE IT WAS MANUALLY CORRECTED USING THE AILERON CONTROL WHEEL. THE AIRCRAFT RECOVERED AND NO OTHER CONTROL PROBLEMS WERE NOTED. THE SPEED BRAKE HANDLE WAS DOWN, THERE WERE NO TRIM INPUTS PRIOR TO THE EVENT AND NO UNUSUAL WHEEL OR RUDDER FORCES WERE NOTED. THE CREW WENT THROUGH THE ABNORMAL PROCEDURE, DISCONNECTED THE YAW DAMPER, BUT DID NOT SHUT OFF HYDRAULICS DUE TO THIS INCIDENT NOT BEING A "RUDDER HARDOVER." UNITED AIRLINES ORD MAINTENANCE, IN COORDINATION WITH LINE ENGINEERING AND FLIGHT SAFETY TROUBLESHOT AND CONDUCTED A THOROUGH AND EXHAUSTIVE CHECK AND INSPECTION OF ALL RELATED FLIGHT CONTROL SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS. THE PRIMARY GUIDANCE FOR THIS TROUBLESHOOTING WAS BOEINGS SERVICE LETTER NUMBER 737-SL-27-110-A, DATED 14 SEPTEMBER 2001. SUBJECT: "UNEXPECTED ROLL AND YAW EVENT TROUBLESHOOTING." AS PART OF THE TROUBLESHOOTING PROCEDURES AND RESULTING INSPECTION AND CHECKS OF THE SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS, THE FOLLOWING COMPONENTS WERE REMOVED AND REPLACED PER THE MAINTENANCE MANUAL: FLIGHT DATA RECORDER, MAIN RUDDER POWER CONTROL UNIT. STANDBY RUDDER ACTUATOR AND THE YAW DAMP COUPLER. IN ADDITION, DURING THE RUDDER ACTUATION CHECK, A BINDING PULLEY WAS NOTED IN THE FORWARD CARGO PIT CEILING AND IT WAS REPLACED. ALL RELATED HYDRAULIC FILTERS WERE REPLACED AND FLUID SAMPLES FROM THE A AND B HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS WERE TAKEN FOR ANALYSIS. DURING THE SYSTEM CHECK OUTS AND TROUBLESHOOTING OF THE RUDDERS (PCU) MAIN POWER CONTROL UNIT, IT WAS NOTED THAT IT DID NOT HAVE A CONSISTENT NEUTRAL. AFTER "SHAKE-OUT" THE RUDDER WOULD RETURN TO A DIFFERENTNEUTRAL EACH TIME WITH A TENDENCY TOWARD THE RIGHT 3/4 INCH. IN ADDITION DURING THIS CHECK OUT THE STAND BY RUDDER ACTUATOR WAS FOUND TO HAVE AN INCONSISTENT FREE-PLAY AND A NEUTRAL 3/4 INCH TO THE LEFT. BOTH OF THESE UNITS WERE SUBSEQUENTLY REPLACED. IN CONCLUSION, THE RUDDER POWER CONTROL UNIT, YAW DAMP COUPLER, AND THE STANDBY RUDDER ACTUATOR WERE REPLACED DUE TO DISCREPANCIES AND AS A PRECAUTION AS RECOMMENDED BY UNITED AIRLINES FLIGHT SAFETY AND ENGINEERING. NO DEFINITE CONCLUSIONS HAVE YET BEEN REACHED AS TO THE SPECIFIC CAUSE FOR THIS UNCOMMANDED ROLL. ALL OF THE DATA HAS NOT BEEN EVALUATED YET, SUCH AS THE RADAR DATA, VOICE RECORDER, OR QAR (QUICK ACCESS RECORDER). THE REMOVED COMPONENTS HAVE BEEN SENT TO UNITED AIRLINES SHOPS FOR TEAR DOWN AND EVALUATION, A FINAL REPORT WITH A CONCLUSION WILL BE PROVIDED BY UNITED AIRLINES AT A LATER DATE. THE SUBJECT AIRCRAFT, N307UA, B737-322 WAS RELEASED FOR SERVICE ON AUGUST 19, 2002 AND AT THE TIME OF THIS REPORT HAD EXPERIENCED NO DIFFICULTIES.

SHORTLY AFTER THE AIRCRAFT LANDED ON RUNWAY 4RIGHT, EMERGENCY VEHICLES MET THE AIRCRAFT BUT WERE NOT NEEDED SINCE THE LANDING WAS UNEVENTFUL EXCEPT FOR SOME DAMAGE TO THE NOSE LANDING GEAR ASSEMBLY. (-23) ON JANUARY 16, 2002 AT APPROXIMATELY 2245, UALA, A320 AIRCRAFT NUMBER 4675 (N475UA) WAS BEING TAXIED BY A UNITED AIRLINES MAINTENANCE TAXI CREW, LINDSEY E. WALKER (LEFT SEAT) AND MICHELLE RUTHKOWSKI (RIGHT SEAT) FROM TERMINAL GATE B-10 TO THE HANGAR FOR THE OVERNIGHT. WEATHER CONDITIONS AT THE TIME WERE TEMPERATURE +27 DEGREES, WINDS FROM 300 @13, GUSTING TO 21. THE RAMP CONDITIONS CONSISTED OF SNOW AND ICE. AS THE AIRCRAFT WAS TAXIING SOUTH TOWARDS THE E-GATES NEAR THE SOUTH PORT, AND AS THE AIRCRAFT STARTED THE RIGHT TURN, THE NOSE WHEEL LOST TRACTION ON THE SNOW COVERED AND ICY RAMP. THE TAXI CREW WAS UNABLE TO CONTROL THE AIRCRAFT AND IT CONTINUED A TURNING SKID TO THE LEFT OF THE TAXI CONTROL LINE. THE LEFT WING OF AIRCRAFT 4675 CONTACTED THE TAIL OF A CONTINENTAL AIRLINES B-757, N17126 PARKED AT GATE E-12. THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A STOP WITH THE WING TIP APPROXIMATELY 45 FEET PAST THE TAIL OF N17216, AIRCRAFT 4675'S WING HAD GONE UNDER THE APU DOORS AREA OF THE B-757 TAIL AND THE AIRCRAFT SKIDDED APPROXIMATELY 250 FEET AND WAS NOW APPROXIMATELY 96 FEET TO THE LEFT OF THE TAXI LINE TOWARDS THE E-GATES. DAMAGE TO 4675 WAS LIMITED TO THE #1 LEADING EDGE SLAT, LEFT WINGTIP FENCE, LEFT WING TIP, LEFT AILERON, AND THE OUTBOARD UNDER WING PANEL. THE CONTINENTAL B-757 HAD DAMAGE TO THE APU DOORS AND THE FUSELAGE SKIN 106 INCHES PAST THE DOORS. THE CONTINENTAL AIRLINES AIRCRAFT WAS FERRIED OUT OF ORD TO HOUSTON FOR REPAIRS THE MORNING OF JANUARY 17, 2002. DURING A CONVERSATION WITH THE CONTINENTAL B-757 PILOT BEFORE THE AIRCRAFT WAS FERRIED TO HOUSTON, THE PILOT STATED THAT THEY WERE AT THE GATE, FULLY LOADED WITH 122 PASSENGERS, 3 CABIN CREW AND 2 COCKPIT CREW. THEY HAD THE CABIN DOOR CLOSED TO KEEP THE HEAT IN WHILE THEY WAITED FOR MAINTENANCE TO COMPLETE SOME LAST MINUTE WORK ON NUMBER 2 ENGINE. THE PILOT ALSO COMMENTED THAT HE FELT THE AIRCRAFT SHUDDER WHEN IT WAS STRUCK, EVEN THOUGH HE HAD NO IDEA WHAT HAD HAPPENED BUT WAS SURE SOMETHING HAD STRUCK HIS AIRCRAFT WHEN HE FELT THE IMPACT. UNITED AIRLINES MAINTENANCE TOWED AIRCRAFT 4675 TO THE HANGAR WHERE IT WAS INSPECTED AND REPAIRED. THE FOLLOWING ITEMS WERE DAMAGED AND REPLACED: #5 LEADING EDGE SLAT, LEFT WING TIP, LEFT WING TIP FENCE AND THE LEFT OUTBOARD WING AILERON. THE OUTBOARD WING STRUCTURE WAS ALSO INSPECTED COMPLETELY AND NO SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE TO IT WAS NOTED. ALL REPAIRS WERE COMPLETED AS OF JANUARY 28, 2002 AND THE AIRCRAFT DEPARTED ON IT'S FIRST REVENUE FLIGHT ON JANUARY 29, 2002. THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT FURTHER REPORTED FLAMES EMITTING FROM THE VIDEO CONTROL UNIT LOCATED RIGHT SIDE MID-CABIN AND A LOUD BANG IN THE MID-CABIN AREA. DURING THIS TIMEFRAME THE PILOT NOTICED MILD RUDDER AND PITCH INPUTS. THE PILOT DECLARED AN EMERGENCY AND THE AIRCRAFT WAS TURNED BACK TO SEATTLE. CIRCUIT BREAKERS WERE PULLED FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM, SMOKE AND ALLEGED FIRE OF THE VIDEO CONTROL UNIT EXTINGUISHED. CABIN FIRE EXTINGUISHER WAS NOT REQUIRED, HOWEVER, THE FIRE EXTINGUISHER WAS REMOVED FROM ITS HOLDER AND WAS READY FOR USE. THE PILOT ALSO REPORTED NUMEROUS INDICATION LIGHTS ILLUMINATED INCLUDING THE LEADING AND TRAILING EDGE LIGHTS, RIGHT AUTO-PILOT, CONTROL WHEEL STEERING AND LANDING GEAR INDICATION LIGHTS. TWO ATTEMPS TO ENGAGE LEFT AUTOPILOT RESULTED IN A SLIGHT PITCH-UP FOLLOWED AUTOPILOT DISENGAGE. DURING BLOCK-IN PILOT NOTICED RIGHT INDICATOR LIGHT CIRCUIT BREAKER POPPED AND AUTO-THROTTLES NOT FUNCTIONING PROPERLY. PASSENGERS DISEMBARKED THE AIRCRAFT USING JET WAY; EMERGENCY EVACUATION WAS NOT EXECUTED. NO REPORTS OF PASSENGERS REQUIRING MEDICAL ASSISTANCE. PILOTS DEBRIEFED DELTA AIRLINES MAINTENANCE IN SEATTLE AND LOGBOOK ENTRIES WERE MADE. THE VIDEO CONTROL UNIT AND VIDEO ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT ASSEMBLY WERE REPLACED. INSPECTION OF THE VIDEO CONTROL CENTER DID NOT REVEAL EVIDENCE OF SMOKE OR FIRE RESIDUE. THE ALLEGED FIRE APPEARED TO HAVE BEEN CONTAINED IN THE VIDEO CONTROL UNIT. ALSO, THE ELECTRICAL SHORT THAT DAMAGED THE ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT ASSEMBLY DID NOT CAUSE SIGNIFICANT COLLATERAL DAMAGE TO COMPONENTS, MATERIAL OR STRUCTURE. CHECKS WERE PERFORMED ON THE AUTOPILOT SYSTEM, FLAPS AND SLATS, ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM, AND PRESSURIZATION SYSTEM. AIRCRAFT WAS PRESSURIZED TO 6 PSI AND CABIN PRESSURE CONTROLLER CHECKED GOOD. THE ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM CHECKED GOOD WITH THE REPLACED VIDEO CONTROL UNIT AND ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT ASSEMBLY, HOWEVER, THE SYSTEM WAS DE-ACTIVATED AND PLACARDED AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE. THE COCKPIT VOICE RECORDER AND FLIGHT DATA RECORDERS WERE REMOVED FROM THE AIRCRAFT AND REPLACED AS AN ADDITIONAL PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE TO PRESERVE THE DATA. SEATTLE MAINTENANCE ALSO REPLACED CIRCUIT CARDS M-10266 AND M-10267 AT THE REQUEST OF DELTA MAINTENANCE CONTROL. THE DAMAGED VIDEO CONTROL BOX AND ANNUNCIATOR LIGHT WERE TAGGED AND ROUTED TO DELTA'S MAIN MAINTENANCE FACILITIES IN ATLANTA FOR EVALUATION. DELTA AIRLINES FAA PRINCIPAL AVIONICS INSPECTOR, NICK PEARSON, IS AWARE OF THIS INCIDENT AND HAD BEEN BRIEFED AS TO OUR FINDINGS. MR. PEARSON NOTED HE WILL FOLLOW-UP ON THE INCIDENT. THE AIRCRAFT WAS RETURNED FOR SERVICE IN SEATTLE ON MARCH 4, 2003, AND DEPARTED TO CINCINNATI (CVG) ON MARCH 5, 2003, AND LANDED WITH NO MAINTENANCE WRITE-UPS.

CALLED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANTS ON THE INTERPHONE AND TOLD THEM TO BE "ALERT" AND THAT THEY MIGHT BE EVACUATING. ANOTHER AIRCRAFT REPORTED TO UAL 1854 THAT THEY HAD A NOSE GEAR FIRE AND SAW FLAMES. (-23) THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT WAS INITIALLY DESCRIBED AS UNRULY BECAUSE SHE HAD AN ALTERCATION WITH THE GATE AGENT IN LA CROSSE (LSE) AS A RESULT OF A PASSENGER COMPLAINT. SHE WAS DRUG/ALCOHOL TESTED UPON HER ARRIVAL IN MSP BY THE COMPANY AND THE RESULTS WERE NEGATIVE. THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM HER FURTHER TRIPS PENDING RECEIPT OF THE TEST RESULTS. PINNACLE FLIGHT ATTENDANT BASE MANAGEMENT COUNSELED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT ON HER APPEARANCE, HYGIENE AND ATTITUDE. THE PINNACLE CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT OFFICE WAS INFORMED ABOUT THE SITUATION AND PLANS NO FURTHER ACTION. AS AN INDEPENDENT ACTION, THE AIRCRAFT, UPON LANDING AT LSE SUSTAINED A BLOWN TIRE AS A RESULT OF A PUNCTURE. THERE WAS NO RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT'S CONDUCT AND THE BLOWN TIRE.
